transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess… I’m here because since my friend was killed, I’ve been carrying this mix of guilt and fear and anger. It just hasn’t let up the way people seemed to think it would.
Have you felt guilty about things that happened even before your friend's death, or has the guilt been focused mostly on what happened to your friend?

Mostly about what happened to her. I keep going over it… like if I’d chosen a different route, or pushed more about that crossing, maybe she’d still be here. And then I get angry again—at the driver, at the town—for letting it happen.
Since your friend’s death, have you noticed a constant low mood or loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of thinking about what happened?

Yes… I suppose I have. I used to fuss over my garden plans, quilt with the ladies, go to the theater sometimes, book club… all that. Now I see it on the calendar and it just feels sort of blank. Like those things belonged to someone else.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend's death?
Yes… most days, it’s there. I don’t know if I’d call it just “depressed,” exactly. It’s more this heavy mix of guilt and fear and anger that hasn’t really let up since she was killed.
Have you experienced days where it was hard to get out of bed, or you felt like nothing mattered anymore?
Some days, yes. I’ll see things on the calendar—gardening, quilting, book club, even the theater—and I just… don’t feel much about them anymore. Like they were for a different version of me.
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like gardening or quilting, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore?

Yes. I used to really get into planning the garden beds, and quilting with the ladies… even book club, the theater. Now I see them written down and I just feel almost nothing. Like those things belonged to who I used to be.
Have you felt unusually tired or noticed that you don’t have the energy to do things you normally could since your friend’s death?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’m older, so I get tired sometimes anyway. I haven’t paid much attention to whether it’s different.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or thinking clearly since your friend's death?

Yes… a bit. When I try to go over the senior-center budget, or even just read a program schedule, the numbers and dates sort of run together. I have to check the same simple thing again and again, like my mind won’t quite hold onto it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight since your friend's death? Like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
I haven’t really noticed anything clear with that. My appetite’s maybe… about the same, as far as I can tell. I don’t think my weight has changed much, but I haven’t been watching it closely.
Have you been feeling like you’re a bad person or felt excessive guilt, even beyond what happened with your friend?
I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, I’ve had thoughts about what happened, but I wouldn’t say I feel like I’m a bad person beyond that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since your friend's death, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t kept track of it closely. Some nights are better than others, I suppose, but I don’t know that I’d call it a big change.
Doctor: Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend's death, even beyond specific moments of sadness?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say it’s most of the day nearly every day. I have sad moments, of course, but I’m not sure I’d call it depressed like that.
Would you say that most days, for most of the day, your mood has been down or depressed, rather than just having occasional sad moments?
I don’t think I’d say that, no. I have times when I feel sad, but… not most of the day most days, I don’t think.
Would you say that most days, for most of the day, your mood has been down or depressed, rather than just having occasional sad moments?
I… I think I already sort of answered that. I have sad spells, yes, but I wouldn’t say it’s most days for most of the day. I’m not really sure how else to put it.
Would you say that, most days, your sadness or low mood lasts for most of the day, even when there's nothing specific happening to make you feel that way?
No… I don’t think it lasts most of the day like that. It comes and goes. I haven’t really noticed it being there all day for no reason.
Would you say that most days, your low mood lasts for most of the day, even when you're not specifically thinking about your friend's death?
No… I don’t think so. It’s not like it stays low most of the day when I’m not thinking about that. I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Would you say that most days, your mood has been low for no clear reason, even when you’re not thinking about your friend’s death or the events around it?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can feel low sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being most days for no clear reason.
Would you say that there have been days when your mood was low for most of the day, even when nothing in particular was happening to make you feel that way?
Maybe a day here or there, but I can’t really say it’s been like that… not for most of the day with no reason. I haven’t kept track.

Over the past two weeks, have there been at least several days in a row where you felt down or had little interest in doing things for most of the day, nearly every day, even when you weren’t thinking about your friend’s death?

I… I don’t know about several days in a row exactly. But I have had that thing where I look at things I used to care about—my garden plans, quilting, book club—and I just feel… nothing much. Like they’re on someone else’s calendar.
